title: New hospital building, Brisbane: live hospital connections
workplace: New 10 storey hospital building with a two level basement and rooftop helipad, on an existing hospital campus next to the live hospital, Brisbane
note: Facts are example inputs for testing. On a real project they come from the contractor's own procedures and the project's documents.

swms.title: Opening into the existing hospital for the link bridge
swms.task: Saw cut and core drill an opening through the existing hospital's load-bearing concrete wall to connect the new link bridge, next to occupied wards, with the wall propped to the engineer's design before cutting.

facts.temporarySupport: The wall is propped to the engineer's design PR-05 (revision A), installed and checked by the engineer before cutting starts.
facts.silicaControls: Cutting and coring are done wet with water-fed saws and core drills, inside a sealed enclosure with the hospital side kept under negative pressure. Fit tested P2 respirators are worn while cutting. The written silica assessment is done before work starts and attached to this SWMS.

steps: Core drill through the slab or wall
Work next to the live hospital
Cut an opening in a load-bearing wall

rules.source: Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 422, s 427, s 447, s 450, s 456
rules.quote: must obtain a copy of the asbestos register from the person with management or control of the workplace, before the person commences the demolition or refurbishment
